summary.text: 比 commonly means “compare” or “match.” Its early Shang use is attested in 王比望乘, but the phrase has competing interpretations, including “follow,” “form an alliance,” and “assist.”

formation.text: The graph’s formation is disputed. One interpretation sees two people side by side, suggesting juxtaposition; the Han dictionary explains it as two 人 forms reversed from 从. A competing proposal connects it with two 匕-like forms. 匕 and 比 have similar reconstructed Old Chinese readings in the Baxter–Sagart system, but that resemblance alone does not establish a phonetic role or what the early graph depicted.

components.text: One interpretation treats the whole graph as two people side by side. The referent of the early form remains disputed.
A competing proposal connects the graph with two 匕 signs, understood as food-taking utensils. The phonetic role of 匕 in 比 is not established.

sound.text: In the Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese system, 匕 *pijʔ resembles 比 *C.pijʔ. This makes a sound link possible but does not prove 匕 was a phonetic component.

components.text: The Han dictionary analyzes 比 as two 人 forms reversed from 从. This historical interpretation is not confirmed by the cited early-script analyses.

history.text: A character study reports several Shang forms, later graphic variation, and continuity in the graph’s basic structure. The sequence of forms does not by itself identify what the graph depicts.

The Han dictionary explains 比 as two 人 forms reversed from 从. Other interpretations see a person-like form or propose two 匕-like forms; the early graph’s referent and component analysis remain disputed.

uncertainties.text: The early graph’s referent and any phonetic role for 匕 remain unsettled. The cited early forms have not been individually verified, and the argument of a 1948 study could not be checked.
The relationship between the early Shang use and later senses is unclear: the Shang phrase has competing readings, and the classical examples do not establish a dated sequence of meanings.

senses.text: In the early Shang phrase 王比望乘, 比 has been read as “follow” or “lead,” “form a close alliance,” or “assist” and “support.” Its precise sense is disputed.

senses.gloss: associate with; attach to a group or person
senses.text: A classical passage is conventionally understood as referring to partial association or factional attachment. A dictionary also records association and following uses, without establishing when they arose.
比 is used to compare or match. In a poem it describes matching a team of horses, but this example does not date the sense’s beginning or show how it relates chronologically to other meanings.
A Zhouyi commentary glosses 比 as “assist” or “support.” This resembles one proposed reading of the Shang phrase, whose meaning remains disputed.
One reconstruction table distinguishes a reading glossed “combine; all” from the reading glossed “compare.” It does not establish how these uses relate or when they arose.

developments.text: Some interpretations connect the Shang use with later association, but the early phrase is disputed, so this development cannot be established.
“Assist” or “support” is one reading of the Shang phrase, but other interpretations differ; it cannot be established as an earlier stage of the later gloss.

limitations.text: Separate dictionary glosses and classical examples do not establish a chronological sequence among the senses. The dates of the specific written witnesses remain unresolved.
